title: Spora Plugin Manifest
description:
Schema for plugin.json — the manifest every Spora plugin ships at its package root.

This mirrors the contract Spora\Plugins\PluginLoader enforces at boot: only `slug` and `class` are hard-required, and a manifest missing either (or carrying a non-string value) is rejected with PluginLoadFailedException before the rest of the application boots. Every other field is optional.

`additionalProperties: false` is deliberate, not incidental. The loader *silently ignores* manifest keys it does not recognise, so a typo (`autoloadd`, `desciption`) would quietly do nothing at runtime. This schema is the only surface that can tell an author their key is unknown. If a plugin genuinely needs a new manifest field, add it here first — do not invent a key.

Intentionally NOT accepted: `version`. No in-tree manifest declares one and no runtime code reads one. The operator-facing version comes from the git tag Composer recorded at install time (Composer\InstalledVersions::getPrettyVersion()); a hand-edited manifest version could only drift from the release operators actually see. `dependencies` is likewise a composer.json concern (Composer `require`), and the old `file` entry-point override was removed when the loader became PSR-4-only.

Human-readable reference: docs.spora-ai.com/reference/plugin-schema. This file is validated against every real plugin manifest in the tree by the `check:plugin-schema` CI job, so it cannot silently drift from what plugins actually ship.

$schema.description: Absolute URI of the schema this manifest validates against, so editors (VSCode json-language-service, JetBrains, ajv) and CI tooling can resolve the contract without a network round-trip. Every manifest in the spora-ai org points at the published copy: "https://docs.spora-ai.com/schemas/plugin.schema.json". No Spora runtime code reads this key — it exists purely for tooling, and is safe to omit.

slug.description: Unique machine-readable identifier for this plugin. Used as the component key in schema_versions and as the required prefix for migration filenames. Must be stable across releases. The loader applies this same pattern at boot and throws PluginLoadFailedException on a violation, so a slug that validates here also boots.

class.description: Fully-qualified class name of the plugin entry point. Must implement Spora\Plugins\PluginInterface. The loader instantiates it via PSR-4 after registering the manifest's `autoload` block, and throws PluginLoadFailedException at boot if the class is missing, unresolvable, or not a PluginInterface.

name.description:
Package / human-readable name for the plugin. In practice every manifest that ships it sets it to the Composer package name from the plugin's composer.json — e.g. "spora-ai/spora-plugin-typst".

No runtime code reads it: PluginLoader keys plugins by `slug` and instantiates `class`, and PluginManager's inventory prefers composer.json#name (falling back to the directory basename for partial installs). Keep it in sync with composer.json — it is here for registry metadata, release tooling, and humans reading the file.

description.description: Short human-readable description of the plugin, surfaced by the inventory UI.

icon.description:
Icon for the plugin in the inventory UI. Two forms are accepted (resolution order: bundled name → raw path). The frontend falls back to a bundled "puzzle" icon if the value is empty (or whitespace-only) or doesn't match either form.

  • Bundled name: a kebab-case identifier from the Spora palette (e.g. "puzzle", "brain", "lightbulb", "compass", "globe"). See docs/07_plugins.md § Bundled icons for the full list.
  • Raw SVG path: a single path string starting with a path command letter (M/L/H/V/C/S/Q/T/A/Z). Smallest in JSON, but limited to single-path icons (use subpaths via `M` to compose multi-shape glyphs).

Full <svg>...</svg> blobs are no longer accepted — the frontend's Icon component used to sanitise them through DOMPurify's SVG profile, but historical mXSS bypasses in that profile motivated dropping the v-html path entirely. Plugin authors should ship a single `d` string.

Defaults to "puzzle" when omitted.

accent.description: Tile accent colour for the plugin's app tile. Mirror the enum in the host's `tileAccent()` map. Precedence: PHP `App::accent()` > this field > `"primary"`. Unknown / missing values fall back to `"primary"` silently.

autoload.description:
Autoloading hints for a plugin that is not — or not only — wired through its own composer.json. Both keys are optional. The loader registers whatever it finds here *after* composer.json's own autoloader is already registered, so these entries act as an override/extension rather than a replacement.

Prefer declaring PSR-4 mappings in composer.json. The manifest block is the escape hatch for sibling-clone workflows and for pointing at a non-Composer source tree.

psr-4.description: PSR-4 namespace-prefix → path mapping, with paths relative to the plugin root. Every entry is handed to Composer's ClassLoader::addPsr4() before the entry-point class is resolved, so a wrong prefix here is what produces a "declares class X but the class is not autoloadable" PluginLoadFailedException at boot. Prefixes conventionally end in a backslash and paths conventionally end in a slash. Multiple entries are supported.

files.description: PHP files to require_once, relative to the plugin root, processed after the psr-4 mappings. This is how a plugin with its own Composer dependency tree loads it: ["vendor/autoload.php"]. Each path is require_once'd only if it exists on disk, so a missing file is skipped silently rather than raising.

frontendEntry.description:
Path to a pre-built frontend bundle this plugin contributes, which lets a JSON-only plugin ship a UI without writing PHP. Read by AppsController::resolveFrontendEntry() as a fallback only: a plugin whose App class implements VueAppInterface has its PHP-declared entry win, and this key is consulted just for the apps that do not.

No manifest in the spora-ai org ships this key yet. It is declared here because the runtime reads it — a plugin that sets it must not be rejected as an unknown key.
